title: Pressure in Fluids
description: Calculate pressure using p = F/A and pressure at depth p = hρg, and explain upthrust and floating.
hero_image_caption: A pressure gradient drives every fluid system — from the crushing depths of the ocean to the gentle buoyancy of a floating boat.
content_html:
What Is Pressure?

Pressure is defined as the force acting normally (at right angles) to a surface divided by the area over which that force acts. The equation is: $$p = \frac{F}{A}$$ where \(p\) is pressure in pascals (Pa), \(F\) is the force in newtons (N), and \(A\) is the area in square metres (m²). A smaller contact area means greater pressure for the same force — which is why a sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt one, and why snowshoes spread your weight to stop you sinking.

Key Fact

Pressure (Pa) = Force (N) ÷ Area (m²). One pascal equals one newton per square metre. Always convert cm² to m² before substituting into the equation (1 cm² = 1 × 10⁻⁴ m²).

Pressure in Liquids and at Depth

In a fluid, pressure acts in all directions and increases with depth. This is because a deeper column of liquid has a greater weight pressing down on any surface below it. The equation linking pressure to depth is: $$p = h\rho g$$ where \(h\) is the height (depth) of the liquid column in metres (m), \(\rho\) (rho) is the density of the liquid in kg/m³, and \(g\) is the gravitational field strength (10 N/kg near Earth’s surface). This equation applies to both liquids and gases.

A common error is forgetting to convert units before substituting. Depth in centimetres must be converted to metres, and density given in g/cm³ must be converted to kg/m³ (multiply by 1000). For example, water has a density of 1 g/cm³, which is 1000 kg/m³ — always use kg/m³ in this equation.

Question: A diver is 25 m below the surface of seawater (density 1025 kg/m³). Calculate the pressure due to the seawater column at this depth. Take \(g\) = 10 N/kg.

Step 1: Identify the values. \(h\) = 25 m, \(\rho\) = 1025 kg/m³, \(g\) = 10 N/kg.

Step 2: Substitute into \(p = h\rho g\).
\(p = 25 \times 1025 \times 10\)
\(p = 256\,250\) Pa

Step 3: State the answer with units. The pressure due to the water column is 256 250 Pa (or approximately 256 kPa). Note: total pressure would also include atmospheric pressure acting on the surface, but the equation \(p = h\rho g\) gives the pressure due to the fluid column only.

Upthrust and Floating

Because pressure in a fluid increases with depth, the pressure acting on the bottom of a submerged object is always greater than the pressure acting on its top. This pressure difference produces a net upward force called upthrust. The magnitude of the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced by the object — a relationship known as Archimedes’ principle.

An object floats when the upthrust equals its weight. If upthrust is less than weight, the object sinks. An object that is less dense than the surrounding fluid will float because it only needs to displace a volume of fluid equal to its own weight before upthrust balances gravity. A steel ship floats not because steel is less dense than water, but because the hollow hull displaces a large volume of water whose weight matches the total weight of the ship.

Key Fact

An object floats when upthrust = weight. Upthrust arises because pressure increases with depth, so the upward force on the bottom face of a submerged object is always greater than the downward force on the top face.

Atmospheric Pressure

Atmospheric pressure is caused by the weight of the air column above Earth’s surface acting on a unit area. Because the atmosphere becomes less dense at altitude (fewer air molecules above), atmospheric pressure decreases with height above the surface. At sea level, atmospheric pressure is approximately 101 000 Pa. This is why ears ‘pop’ when travelling up a mountain or in a descending aircraft: the external pressure changes, creating a temporary pressure difference across the eardrum.

The same principle explains how a drinking straw works: reducing the air pressure inside the straw (by breathing in) allows the higher atmospheric pressure outside to push the liquid up. This is often incorrectly described as ‘suction pulling the liquid’ — in reality, the liquid is pushed by the pressure difference.

Question: A hydraulic piston exerts a force of 4500 N over a circular surface of area 0.03 m². Calculate the pressure produced.

Step 1: Identify values. \(F\) = 4500 N, \(A\) = 0.03 m².

Step 2: Substitute into \(p = \frac{F}{A}\).
\(p = \frac{4500}{0.03} = 150\,000\) Pa

Step 3: State with units: 150 000 Pa (or 150 kPa).

Rearranging for force: \(F = p \times A\). Rearranging for area: \(A = \frac{F}{p}\). Always include units in your final answer — a common exam error is omitting them.

Gas Pressure and the Particle Model

In a gas, pressure arises from the random collisions of gas molecules with the walls of their container. Increasing the temperature of a fixed volume of gas gives molecules more kinetic energy, so they hit the walls harder and more frequently — pressure increases. Compressing the gas into a smaller volume (at constant temperature) means more frequent collisions per unit area — again, pressure increases. At constant temperature: \(p \times V = \text{constant}\) (Boyle’s law). Doubling the pressure halves the volume.
exam_tip_html: In calculation questions using \(p = h\rho g\), the most common errors are failing to convert cm to m (divide by 100) and g/cm³ to kg/m³ (multiply by 1000). Always write the conversion step explicitly. For ‘explain floating’ questions, you must link pressure difference with depth to the upward force — saying ‘light objects float’ scores no marks. The exam also asks you to explain why atmospheric pressure decreases with height: the key phrase is ‘fewer air molecules above, so less weight of air acting on a unit area’.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Pressure = Force ÷ Area (Pa = N/m²). Always convert area to m² before calculating.
  • Pressure at depth in a fluid: \(p = h\rho g\). Pressure increases with depth, density, and gravitational field strength.
  • Upthrust is the net upward force on a submerged object caused by the pressure difference between its bottom and top faces. An object floats when upthrust equals its weight.

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following correctly states the equation for pressure?
A) p = F × A
B) p = A / F
C) p = F / A
D) p = F × A²
State the SI unit of pressure and give its equivalent in base SI units.
practice_questions.marks: Pascal (Pa); equivalent to N/m² (newton per square metre). [1 mark — accept either]

practice_questions.text: Describe how pressure in a liquid changes with depth, and explain why this change occurs.
practice_questions.marks: Pressure increases with depth (1). This is because there is a greater weight of liquid above acting on a given area / a greater column of liquid above pressing down (1). [2 marks]

practice_questions.text: Explain why a steel ship floats even though steel is denser than water.
practice_questions.marks: The hollow hull of the ship displaces a large volume of water (1). The weight of water displaced equals the total weight of the ship (1). The upthrust produced equals the ship’s weight, so the ship floats / upthrust = weight (1). [3 marks]

practice_questions.text:
A submarine is 80 m below the surface of seawater. The density of seawater is 1025 kg/m³ and g = 10 N/kg.
(a) Calculate the pressure due to the seawater column at this depth.
(b) The submarine’s hull has a surface area of 420 m² on its upper face at this depth. Calculate the force exerted by the water on this surface.
practice_questions.marks:
(a) p = hρg = 80 × 1025 × 10 = 820 000 Pa (2 marks: 1 for correct substitution, 1 for correct answer with units)
(b) F = p × A = 820 000 × 420 = 344 400 000 N = 3.44 × 10⁸ N (2 marks: 1 for correct rearrangement and substitution, 1 for correct answer with units) [4 marks total]

practice_questions.text: A student claims: ‘When you drink through a straw, suction pulls the liquid up.’ Evaluate this claim, referring to the concept of atmospheric pressure and the pressure difference created inside the straw.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (5–6 marks): Correctly identifies that ‘suction’ is a misleading description. Explains that breathing in reduces the air pressure inside the straw. States that atmospheric pressure acting on the liquid surface outside the straw is now greater than the pressure inside. Explains that this pressure difference produces a net upward force on the liquid, pushing it up the straw. Refers to the liquid being pushed rather than pulled. May note that atmospheric pressure at sea level is approximately 101 000 Pa and that the pressure difference drives the liquid upwards.
Secure (3–4 marks): Correctly identifies the role of pressure difference. States that pressure inside the straw is reduced, and atmospheric pressure outside is greater. Explains liquid is pushed up, not pulled, but lacks full mechanistic explanation.
Developing (1–2 marks): Recognises that pressure is involved but explanation is incomplete or partially incorrect. [6 marks]

Which row correctly shows how pressure in a liquid changes with depth and density?

Pressure increases with both depth and density
Pressure is not affected by depth or density

flashcard_questions.q: What equation links pressure, force and area?
flashcard_questions.a: p = F ÷ A, where p is pressure in pascals, F is force in newtons, and A is area in square metres.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the equation for the pressure at a given depth in a liquid?
flashcard_questions.a: p = hρg, where h is depth in metres, ρ is the density of the liquid in kg/m³, and g is gravitational field strength in N/kg.

flashcard_questions.q: What is upthrust and what causes it?
flashcard_questions.a: An upward force on a submerged object, caused by the pressure difference between the bottom face (higher pressure, greater depth) and the top face (lower pressure, lesser depth).

flashcard_questions.q: State the condition for an object to float.
flashcard_questions.a: An object floats when the upthrust acting on it equals its weight.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does atmospheric pressure decrease with increasing altitude?
flashcard_questions.a: There are fewer air molecules above a given point, so the weight of the air column above that point — and hence the pressure it exerts — is smaller.

flashcard_questions.q: What unit conversion must you make when using p = hρg if density is given in g/cm³?
flashcard_questions.a: Multiply by 1000 to convert from g/cm³ to kg/m³. For example, 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³.

flashcard_questions.q: How does increasing the temperature of a fixed volume of gas affect its pressure, and why?
flashcard_questions.a: Pressure increases because molecules move faster, collide with the walls more frequently and with greater force, exerting a greater force per unit area.

glossary_terms.definition: The force exerted per unit area, measured in pascals (Pa).
The SI unit of pressure, equal to one newton per square metre (N/m²).
A substance (liquid or gas) that can flow and takes the shape of its container.
Mass per unit volume of a substance, measured in kg/m³.
An upward force on an object immersed in a fluid, caused by the pressure difference between the bottom and top of the object.
To rest on the surface of a fluid, supported by upthrust equal to the object's weight.
The pressure exerted by the weight of the atmosphere above a given point on Earth's surface.
